![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14032117/assets/4e9218dcfc77ec080139f2650ea19f78199557e0ce2d8d53c1996ec0ea6145a6.png)

The half-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=3$ and $b=2.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a half-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the elipse and the $x$-axis. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14032117/assets/dfbe843a9ad0847d7174984fa7c7c48834af48b3ee2335b5383b15f7fb826763.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[\pi ,2\pi ]$, we get the half-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the half-ellipse are 

$$
x=3\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [\pi ,2\pi ].
$$
